sources.entry: OpenTypeless - Open-source AI voice input that types polished text into any app. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/tover0314-w/opentypeless) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: OpenTypeless is an open-source, cross-platform desktop app (macOS, Windows, Linux) that turns speech into polished text typed into any app, and offers hotkey-driven voice Q&A and selected-text rewriting.
keywords: transcribe speech to text in any app
summary.what_it_does: Press a global hotkey, speak, and OpenTypeless transcribes the audio through a configured speech-to-text provider, optionally rewrites it with an LLM, and types or copies the result into the active app. Ask Anything records a one-shot spoken question, sends it to an LLM, and shows only the answer in a small floating panel. Selected-text editing lets you speak an instruction to rewrite, summarize, translate, or fix text selected in another app. A translation shortcut sends output to one of several configured target languages. Supporting features include a local dictionary with correction rules, per-app style mappings, scenes, and local history. Users can bring their own API keys (BYOK) or use an optional managed cloud plan.
use_cases: dictate emails and chat replies by voice
speak text and have it polished before typing
ask a quick voice question without opening a chat app
rewrite or translate selected text by speaking
dictate into any desktop app with a hotkey
run voice input fully offline with a local Whisper and Ollama setup
notable: Ask Anything: shortcut-first one-shot voice Q&A that shows only the final answer, with no chat history
BYOK mode sends audio and text directly to the chosen provider; API keys are kept in the OS credential vault where available
App-aware polish detects the active app locally and sends only an internal category and style metadata to the LLM
Works with many STT providers (Deepgram, AssemblyAI, Groq Whisper, OpenAI Whisper, custom endpoints) and OpenAI-compatible LLMs including Ollama
Native Fn / Right Alt hotkeys on macOS and Windows; Linux uses Ctrl-based defaults and Wayland helpers wtype or kwtype
caveats: Linux Wayland direct typing depends on a compositor-specific helper (kwtype or wtype); global hotkeys can vary by desktop environment
Cloud features require connecting to www.opentypeless.com; BYOK mode avoids this but needs your own provider keys
Release signing differs by platform: Windows SmartScreen warnings and macOS Gatekeeper may block first launch until notarization catches up
Building from source requires Node.js 20+, a stable Rust toolchain, and Tauri platform prerequisites
